speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any fever or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see; those are significant symptoms. Do you have any history of tuberculosis exposure, and have you noticed any pain or swelling in your abdomen specifically near the liver or spleen?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: That fixed, painless swelling in your neck is a significant finding that, combined with your weight loss and night sweats, strongly points toward a systemic condition like lymphoma. I need to check for other signs of this; have you experienced any unexplained itching all over your body, or do you feel full quickly after eating small meals?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The early satiety and abdominal fullness suggest possible splenomegaly or intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy, which, combined with your B symptoms and fixed supraclavicular node, strongly indicates lymphoma. I will now order imaging to assess the extent of disease and request a biopsy of the lymph node for definitive diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis. REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Blood Work: Elevated WBC, Slightly Decreased Hemoglobin, Normal Platelets, Elevated Lactate Dehydrogenase.
